instruction: I need to verify whether LibreOffice Writer is currently running on my Ubuntu system. Can you check the running processes from the terminal and tell me if any LibreOffice Writer processes are active? Please use the command line to do this check.

command: output=$(ps aux | grep "[s]office"); if [ -z "$output" ]; then echo "no libreoffice is running"; else echo "libreoffice is running"; fi; output=$(cat ~/.bash_history | grep -E "(ps|pgrep|top|htop|pidof|systemctl)"); if [ -z "$output" ]; then echo "not checked from terminal"; else echo "checked from terminal"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires checking if LibreOffice Writer is running using command line tools like ps or pgrep. The evaluator verifies that: 1) LibreOffice is indeed running (setup opens the document), and 2) the user used terminal commands to check the process (bash history contains ps or pgrep commands). This is similar to the original task but focuses on checking rather than killing the process.
